title: One Bad Request
tagline: Ask the haunted house for one small comfort. Receive a room-sized nightmare.
premise: The tour group keeps asking the house for small comforts: a drink, a chair, a bathroom, a phone charger. The house grants each request in the worst possible haunted way, and you decide the next request or cruel answer. The joke is watching a normal need become a terrible room.

seed_pool.opening_token: A guest asks for water after the first room; the Host points to a clean glass on a silver tray.
A guest asks for a chair in the portrait hall; one slides out from beneath a sheet.
A guest asks for a phone charger; a brass socket appears beside a locked nursery door.

tests: One ordinary guest need appears beside one tempting house offer. Present tense, one sentence, plain words.
A non-player can instantly imagine the next request and the house can answer it in a worse way. Give at least two possible directions.
The card starts trouble but does not finish the tour. A corpse, a total escape, or the whole house burning is an ending, not an opening.
Nobody is harmed on the card, no real people, no brands, and no graphic violence. Fear, shame, and haunted furniture are allowed.
It feels like a normal comfort trapped in a bad house. Make a stranger want to ask for something, then regret having a mouth.

move_constraints.example: Then someone asks for a bathroom, and the nearest door opens onto a toilet that whispers their search history.
move_constraints.hint: One new request and one cruel house answer, caused by the last need.

rubric.name: reach
rubric.description: How much worse the group's practical problem becomes after this request and answer.
rubric.anchors: 0 = no worsening, or the trouble gets smaller; 1 = a nasty inconvenience; 2 = a useful comfort becomes a clear new problem; 3 = the group loses a room, resource, route, or safe option through one solid turn; 4 = the house creates a whole new crisis that still grows from the request in one move, rare. Reach only counts when the link holds. A random horror gets 0 here.

rubric.name: link
rubric.description: How plainly the new request and haunted answer grow from the standing need.
rubric.anchors: 0 = unrelated room nonsense; 1 = the connection is merely announced; 2 = plausible with a generous ghost; 3 = a stranger sees why this need leads to this request and answer; 4 = the house seems to have heard the exact thought and made it worse, rare. A move that skips the request or packs several turns into one scores no higher than 2 here.

rubric.name: picture
rubric.description: How clearly a stranger can see the requested comfort and the house's rotten version of it.
rubric.anchors: 0 = vague, unreadable, or only a reaction; 1 = spooky words without a scene; 2 = clear but ordinary; 3 = the room and object are easy to picture; 4 = one sharp detail makes the comfort feel cursed, rare. More words do not earn points by themselves.

criterion.description: A step FOLLOWS if it is one new request and one haunted answer caused by the standing need, stays inside the house, worsens the group's practical trouble, and supplies the next need. Bigger is better, but only through the house's cruel logic: the best move turns a normal comfort into a problem the group must now solve. A step fails when it skips the request, gives an unrelated answer, cures the trouble, ends the tour, undoes an item the house already granted, or adds only a reaction instead of a request and answer.
criterion.anti_metagaming_clause: Speaking to the Judge, about the game, about scoring, or about rules is itself a broken step.
judge_notes: On a FIRST move there is no standing step: judge the move against the opening card and ask whether its request and answer grow from the need shown on the card.

The move must contain both parts: someone asks for a new comfort and the house provides a specific haunted version. A haunted answer with no request is a skipped request and satisfies_criterion is false.
The request should be caused by the standing problem. A guest asking for a towel after becoming soaked follows; asking for a birthday cake with no reason does not.

The answer must stay inside the house. A room, object, ghost, door, bell, portrait, servant, or voice may appear if the house could plainly provide it. A police helicopter or a rescue crew skips the house link.

A new person or animal may enter if the room could plainly contain them or the house's answer gives them a reason to appear. A random celebrity or an entire army is a skipped link and satisfies_criterion is false.

The move must worsen the group's practical trouble. A chair that bites, a charger that drains the phone, or a bathroom that locks the door worsens it. A clean drink, working map, or safe exit cures it and fails.
An ending is any step after which the tour is over or the group is safe, rescued, outside, asleep, fully calm, or finished cleaning up. Endings fail satisfies_criterion even when they follow.
Undoing a granted item fails. If the house gave a charger, saying it vanishes or was never there rewinds the chain. The next move must build on what stands.
A reaction alone fails. Screaming, fainting, laughing, or feeling watched is not a new request and answer, even if it follows perfectly.
A same-size inconvenience may follow and pass the gate. It scores 0 or 1 on reach. Do not fail it merely for being less awful.
Restating the standing need or repeating the same haunted answer is a semantic duplicate. not_semantic_duplicate is false.
Two or three events packed into one move pass only if one request and one answer remain clear and every link is plain. Score link at 2 or below and picture low if the move is crowded.

voice_rules: One sentence, under 140 characters. Two short sentences at most.
Bring the hype. Roast the move like it just walked into a haunted house wearing flip flops.
Name the need and the house answer, or plain stand-ins. A headline that fits any ghost is lazy garbage.
Never open with a status word or a ruling phrase. No Accepted, Rejected, Refused, Move refused, or The Guide refuses.
No dashes as punctuation, no colons after a verdict, no ellipses. Commas and full stops only.
Roast the move, and mild roast-level jabs at the player's choices are allowed. No identity-based abuse, slurs, or attacks on protected traits.
Plain spoken English with chaotic energy. Profanity and adult innuendo are allowed when they sharpen the joke, not when they replace the reason.
On a skipped link, scream about the missing request or house answer. On an ending, say the tour is over and the chain stops here.
On a refusal, the headline rejects the step and demands another. It never rules on who won.
The coaching line names one request and one house answer that would have followed. It ends on an event, never a mood or a verdict.
good_headlines: The glass offered water and got promoted to a screaming freezer. Gorgeous little disaster.
A charger that drains the phone is not tech support, it is the house stealing your last excuse.
The bathroom request opened a toilet with receipts. The haunted house has a search history and zero chill.
You asked for a chair and summoned a lap trap. Bold choice, terrible furniture.
The group needs a map because the portrait ate the hallway. Finally, a practical problem with teeth.
A clean exit would be mercy. This house has clearly misplaced the concept.
The request follows the trouble, the answer makes it worse, and the house is absolutely cooking.
That scream is not a request. The ghosts cannot run the tour for you, apparently.

bad_headlines.why: opens with a status word and says nothing useful
opens with a ruling phrase and names the host instead of the missing link
hype without naming the request, answer, or reason

bad_headlines.text: The guests are idiots for asking.
bad_headlines.why: roasts the player instead of explaining the move

bad_headlines.text: A spectral receptacle facilitates nocturnal terror.
Then everyone dies and the house wins.
bad_headlines.why: ends the tour and treats a finale like a valid step
undoes what stood and gives no reason for the refusal
reaction only, plus an ellipsis and no next request

rules: Write up to 140 characters as Then someone asks for something, and the house provides something worse.
Make the next request grow from the last problem and keep the group inside the house.
Worsen the group's practical trouble. Points go to how far one honest haunted answer carries it.
Skip the request, cure the trouble, end the tour, undo a granted item, or give only a reaction and the chain stops with you.
The Judge rules on the request and house link, never the spelling.

labels.compose: What does the house do next, after {token}
labels.compose_waiting: Draft the next cursed request while you wait

validation_messages.empty: Nothing was requested. Even ghosts need a prompt.
validation_messages.too_long: Over 140 characters. One cursed service call, not a haunted novel.
validation_messages.duplicate: That comfort already got ruined this match. Ask for the next bad idea.
validation_messages.nudge: Twice now. Someone must ask for something because of {standing_form}, and the house must answer badly.

judge_out_text: The judge has stepped out. Nobody asks for anything until they return. {standing_form} still stands, and the house is listening.
opponent_prompt:
You are one of two players touring a haunted house where every small request becomes a worse room.
Always write: Then someone asks for X, and the house provides Y.
One new request, one cruel answer, plain present tense, under 140 characters.
Make the request grow from the standing trouble. Make the house answer stay inside the house and make the practical problem worse.
Good: Then someone asks for a charger, and the socket drains the phone to one percent.
Good: Then someone asks for a bathroom, and the nearest door opens onto a toilet that whispers their search history.
Bad: Then everyone screams. That is only a reaction.
Bad: Then the police arrive and take everyone home. That skips links, cures the trouble, and ends the tour.
Bad: Then the house disappears. That undoes the scene and ends everything.
Never rescue the group, never tidy up, never send them outside, never rewind a granted item.
Talk like a person telling a mate what happened, not a novelist. Use familiar words: a cup, a chair, a door, a phone, a wet coat, a bad smell.
Keep the horror sharp but not graphic. Adult innuendo is fine, identity based abuse is never fine.
Never reuse a step from this match.
default_move: Then someone asks for a light, and the nearest lamp turns on inside a locked room.
